achievements.title: First Stamp
achievements.description: Complete the opening room and officially join the route.

achievements.title: Festival Preview
achievements.description: Finish the first three districts and glimpse the routes ahead.

achievements.title: Stage Marks
achievements.description: Finish the Theater district and restore the stamped stage route.

achievements.title: Festival Line
achievements.description: Reconnect the full rooftop delivery lane.

achievements.title: Attic Door
achievements.description: Find the hidden attic route above the town.

achievements.title: Secret Line
achievements.description: Finish the attic postscript and restore Mina's hidden route.

achievements.title: Archivist
achievements.description: Collect every hidden journal thread tucked into the late-game side routes.

achievements.title: Careful Hands
achievements.description: Finish a room without using any hints.

districts.title: Mailroom
districts.subtitle: The first tears in the paper
districts.summary: Learn how stitched sheets overlap, when to transfer a parcel, and how a route can fold back on itself.
districts.journalBody: The storm did not break the town so much as peel it apart. Mina says a good postkeeper does not force paper flat. They learn the folds, the little stubborn bulges, and work with them.

districts.title: Market
districts.subtitle: Routes braided through stalls and awnings
districts.summary: Transfer parcels between layers and use them to hold shutters open, even when the switch is hidden. Ice-slicked corridors add momentum puzzles.
districts.journalBody: The market vendors patched their awnings before their roofs. Priorities. Every route is now tied to every other route, so fixing one usually means fixing three.

districts.title: Greenhouse
districts.subtitle: Lantern light and vine projections
districts.summary: Projection lanterns cast temporary bridges onto neighboring layers, then combine with doors, one-way gates, and multi-sheet routes.
districts.journalBody: Some paper is seeded with silver thread. Mina calls it greenhouse stock. Shine a lamp through it and the next layer blooms into shape.

districts.title: Clocktower
districts.subtitle: Timing made visible
districts.summary: Echo couriers, teleporter shortcuts, rerouted stitch exits, and one optional side route hidden inside the bell frame.
districts.journalBody: The tower's routes are delayed by one bell. If I move now, my echo steps a moment later. It is unsettling to solve puzzles with my own future in the room.

districts.title: Theater
districts.subtitle: Shadows on the backdrops
districts.summary: Shadow couriers latch hidden marks, then combine with ice, one-way gates, and rerouted stitch landings across the stage.
districts.journalBody: Every prop in the theater has a partner behind the curtain. Nothing moves alone, especially not under the footlights.

districts.title: Rooftops
districts.subtitle: The festival line
districts.summary: Projection and transfer stamps reshape the final rooftop lanes before the festival route reconnects. All mechanics converge.
districts.journalBody: When the routes finally align, the whole town reads like one folded letter. Rooftops first, festival after.

districts.title: Attic
districts.subtitle: A hidden route tucked into the rafters
districts.summary: A post-credits secret line opened by the three hidden margin routes across the late game.
districts.journalBody: There is always one route Mina forgets to mention aloud. She says every town deserves one secret line for the people who still look up.

rooms.title: Loose Thread
rooms.objective: Reach the glowing mailbox.
rooms.blurb: The first sheet has peeled away from the second.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: Stitch markers connect identical coordinates. Stand on one and flip the room over.

hintTiers: The front sheet is a winding maze. Find the stitch hidden in the corridors.
Navigate to the center of the front maze, find the stitch at column 4 row 3, then switch layers.
From start go right, right, down, down, right, right, up to reach the stitch. Switch layers, then go right, down, down, right, up to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Teach stitched layer switching through a winding dual-layer maze.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players over-search the front sheet instead of treating the stitch as required progress.

rooms.title: Stamped Twice
rooms.objective: Transfer both parcels and navigate past the blocked corridors to reach the mailbox.
rooms.blurb: Two parcels block the only corridors wide enough for a postkeeper.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: Transfers move a parcel to the same coordinates on the next sheet. You only need the route clear for yourself.

hintTiers: Both parcels block critical corridors. You need to transfer them, not push them into dead ends.
Transfer parcel A first to clear the lower corridor, then navigate up to transfer parcel B and reach the stitch.
Go right twice, transfer parcel A to the back sheet, go up twice, right twice, transfer parcel B, go up to the stitch, switch layers, then navigate down and right to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Teach parcel transfer with three parcels blocking critical corridors.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players try to push parcels into dead ends rather than transferring them between layers.

rooms.title: Forwarding Fold
rooms.objective: Find the one working stitch path through the maze of decoy stitches.
rooms.blurb: Multiple stitches dot both sheets, but only one sequence leads to the mailbox.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: Not every stitch leads somewhere useful. Some drop you into dead ends on the other sheet. Read both sides before you jump.

hintTiers: Three stitches are visible but only one sequence avoids dead ends on the back sheet.
The leftmost stitch drops you into a walled corner. The center stitch is the correct first jump. Then navigate to the second stitch on the back sheet.
Navigate right and up to the center stitch at (4,2), switch layers, go down and left to the lower stitch at (2,5), switch back, then go right to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Teach players to read three layers before committing to a stitch path.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players jump at the first stitch they find and end up trapped.

rooms.title: Return Receipt
rooms.objective: Switch layers three times using the winding stitch network to reach the goal.
rooms.blurb: A side route that rewards noticing every stitch before choosing your path.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: Some routes ask you to fold the room twice before they make sense.

hintTiers: You need to use three different stitches, alternating layers each time.
Start on the front sheet, take the top-left stitch, navigate down on the back sheet to the center stitch, switch back, then find the bottom stitch.
Go right to stitch at (3,1), switch layers, go down through corridors to stitch at (5,4), switch back, navigate left and down to stitch at (2,6), switch layers, go right to mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Teach routes alternating between three sheets with stitch planning.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players reach the first stitch and assume the puzzle is solved.

rooms.title: Backdated Route
rooms.objective: Push parcels onto switches across both layers to open the door blocking the mailbox.
rooms.blurb: The final mailroom route demands parcel management across winding corridors and two layers.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: This one folds back on itself. Clear the lower stitch first, then look for the older route above it.

outro.speaker: Mina
outro.text: Good. The market shutters care less about neat folds and more about what you leave parked on a plate.

hintTiers: One parcel goes on the visible switch, the other must be transferred to the back sheet's switch.
Push parcel A left onto the front switch first, then navigate to parcel B and transfer it to the back sheet where it lands on the hidden switch.

Push parcel A left onto switch at (1,6), go up and right to parcel B, transfer it to the back layer where it lands on the switch at (6,3), use the stitch, navigate through the opened door to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Cap the mailroom with three-layer traversal and triple-switch door logic.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players switch too early without managing all parcels first.

rooms.title: Counterweight
rooms.objective: Slide across ice to reach the switch, park the parcel, and take the opened route.
rooms.blurb: The market lifts its shutters with pressure plates, but the floor is slick with ice.

intro.speaker: Market Clerk
intro.text: Ice corridors slide you until you hit something solid. Plan your approach before you step onto the frost.

hintTiers: The ice corridor slides you all the way across. You need something solid to stop against.
Push the parcel into the ice lane first so it acts as a stopping block, then slide into position near the switch.
Push parcel right onto ice, slide right to stop against it, push it right onto the switch, navigate up to the stitch, switch layers, go through the opened door to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Introduce ice tiles with parcel-as-blocker and dual switches.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players step onto ice without a stopping block.

rooms.title: Stall Shortcut
rooms.objective: Push the parcel across ice to land on the distant plate, then take the shortcut.
rooms.blurb: A side route that asks you to aim a parcel slide precisely.

intro.speaker: Market Clerk
intro.text: The side lane is lighter than the main route. Prop the shutter and steal the short way across.

hintTiers: The parcel must slide across ice and stop exactly on the switch. Plan your push direction.
Push the parcel downward so it slides on ice and stops against the far wall, landing on the switch.
Navigate above the parcel, push it down onto the ice lane where it slides to the switch at (3,6). Use the stitch, switch layers, and cross through the opened door to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Reinforce ice-slide physics with precise parcel aiming.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players push the parcel sideways instead of down the ice column.

rooms.title: Counter Slot
rooms.objective: Use ice lanes and two switches to open the path. One parcel slides, one parks.
rooms.blurb: Some market plates live on the back sheet, far from the player.

intro.speaker: Market Clerk
intro.text: The switch is behind the counter, but the parcel still fits through the slot. Use that instead of looking for another hallway.

hintTiers: Two switches control the door. One is visible on ice, the other is hidden on the back layer.
Slide one parcel across ice onto the visible switch, then transfer the other parcel to land on the hidden switch.

Push parcel A right across ice to the visible switch. Navigate to parcel B and transfer it to the back layer where it lands on the hidden switch. Use the stitch, walk through the opened door to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine ice sliding with cross-layer switch activation using three parcels.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players search for a walking path behind the counter.

rooms.title: Ledger Slip
rooms.objective: Navigate an ice maze that spans both layers, using stitches to bypass blocked corridors.
rooms.blurb: A side room that turns the entire floor into a sliding puzzle across two sheets.

intro.speaker: Market Clerk
intro.text: The back-lane shutter lifts from the same hidden plate, but now you still have to get onto the right sheet.

hintTiers: The ice fills most of both layers. You need walls and stitches as stopping points.
Slide right on ice, stop at the wall, then slide down to the stitch. Switch layers and navigate the back ice maze.
Slide right to wall, slide down to stitch at (7,4), switch layers, slide left to wall at (1,4), slide down to (1,6), slide right to wall, slide up to mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Pure ice navigation puzzle requiring both layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players try to navigate only on one layer.

rooms.title: Inventory Check
rooms.objective: Use ice lanes, two parcels, and two switches across both layers to open the central shutter.
rooms.blurb: The final market route asks you to think about both sheets at once.

intro.speaker: Market Clerk
intro.text: One parcel props the shutter in plain sight. The other has to disappear behind the counter. Sort them before you walk.

outro.speaker: Gardener
outro.text: The greenhouse routes do not stay still either. Bring those steady hands over when you are done here.

hintTiers: You have one parcel for each switch. The ice complicates positioning. Decide which goes where first.
Slide parcel A across ice onto the visible switch. Transfer parcel B to the back sheet where it must be pushed onto the hidden switch. Then use the stitch.

Push parcel A right across ice row to the visible switch at (8,5). Navigate to parcel B and transfer it to back layer. Use the stitch, push the transferred parcel onto the hidden switch at (2,7), then navigate through the opened door to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Cap the market with three-layer parcel management and triple switch logic.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players try to solve the visible plate first.

rooms.title: Paper Vines
rooms.objective: Push the projector into position, navigate one-way gates, and cross the projected bridge.
rooms.blurb: Lanterns draw temporary structure where the paper has torn away. One-way gates restrict your path.

intro.speaker: Gardener
intro.text: Line the lamp up with the tear. The next layer will grow a bridge where the light lands. And mind the one-way gates.

hintTiers: The one-way gates force you to circle around. Push the projector before you commit to the gate path.
Push the projector left to align it with the gap on the other layer, then take the one-way gate circuit to the stitch.
Push projector left to (2,4), go up through the right-only gate, navigate around to the stitch at (3,1), switch layers, follow the one-way path down across the bridge to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Introduce one-way gates alongside projector alignment across three layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players go through one-way gates the wrong direction.

rooms.title: Graft Line
rooms.objective: Combine projector placement with ice sliding and one-way gates to bridge the gap.
rooms.blurb: Not every bridge blooms directly underneath the lantern. Ice complicates the approach.

intro.speaker: Gardener
intro.text: Silver thread bends the light. Sometimes the bloom lands one square away from the lamp itself.

hintTiers: The projector has an offset beam. It bridges one tile away from where it stands.
Slide the projector across ice to the right position, then navigate the one-way gates to the stitch.

Push projector right onto ice where it slides to (5,4). Its offset beam bridges the gap at (6,3) on the back layer. Navigate the one-way loop to the stitch, switch layers, cross the bridge to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine offset projection with ice and one-way gates across three layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players line the lantern up directly instead of accounting for the shifted beam.

rooms.title: Overgrowth
rooms.objective: Project bridges across 3 layers using two projectors to create a connected path.
rooms.blurb: Some greenhouse tears ask for more than a single square of light across multiple sheets.

intro.speaker: Gardener
intro.text: This bed tore wider than the others. Two lamps, three sheets. Every bridge matters.

hintTiers: Each projector bridges a different layer. Position them both before traveling down.
Projector A bridges layer 0 to layer 1. Projector B bridges layer 1 to layer 2. Push both into alignment first.
Push projector A up to (3,2) bridging the gap on layer 1. Push projector B right to (6,4) bridging the gap on layer 2. Use the stitch at top, descend through layers using bridges.

balance.intendedLesson: Three-layer projection requiring two projectors with offset beams.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players align one projector and forget the second bridge.

rooms.title: Misted Gate
rooms.objective: Combine one-way gates, ice, a projector, and a switch to open the path across three layers.
rooms.blurb: The lantern route and the pressure gate have to be solved in the right order.

intro.speaker: Gardener
intro.text: The gate and the vine bridge answer different tools. Set the parcel first so the lamp can do the rest.

hintTiers: The parcel must reach the switch, the projector must bridge the gap, and you must navigate one-way gates in the right order.
Push the parcel across ice onto the switch first, then position the projector, then navigate through the one-way gates to descend through layers.

Push parcel left across ice onto the switch at (1,5). Push projector up to (4,2). Navigate through one-way gates to the top stitch. Descend through middle layer to lower stitch. Cross the bridge through the opened door to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine one-way gates, ice, projection, and dual switches across three layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players try to solve the bridge first.

rooms.title: Festival Draft
rooms.objective: Use two projectors and a parcel across three layers to restore the greenhouse finale route.
rooms.blurb: The final demo room chains parcel parking, projection, and a true three-sheet route.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: The festival draft uses every early trick at once. Hold the gate first, grow the bridge second, then follow the route where the paper is still layered thick.

hintTiers: Treat this like two setup problems before it becomes a travel problem: gate first, lanterns second.
Park the parcel on the switch, push both projectors into their bridge positions, then descend through all three layers.

Push parcel onto switch at (1,8). Push projector A to bridge gap on layer 1. Push projector B to bridge gap on layer 2. Use top stitch, descend through middle layer, use lower stitch, cross both bridges through the opened door to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Cap the demo slice with three-sheet traversal and dual projection.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players keep looking for the goal on the middle sheet.

rooms.title: One Bell Late
rooms.objective: Use the echo courier and a teleporter to hold the door long enough to pass.
rooms.blurb: Your last move returns as a delayed helper, now with teleporter shortcuts.

intro.speaker: Bell Keeper
intro.text: The echo courier repeats your previous move exactly one turn later. Give it a beat to catch up. And the old bell tubes still work.

hintTiers: The echo needs to reach the switch via the teleporter. Time your moves so the echo warps to the right spot.
Move right to queue the echo, wait so it steps onto the teleporter, which sends it near the switch. Then pass through the door.
Walk right, wait for the echo to teleport near the switch, walk right through the opened door, then navigate the maze to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Teach echo timing with teleporter mechanics and gravity tiles.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players move too quickly and forget the echo delay.

rooms.title: Borrowed Bell
rooms.objective: Combine the echo, a parcel, and cross-layer teleporters to open the route.
rooms.blurb: A delayed footstep can hold the route open while the parcel crosses between layers.

intro.speaker: Bell Keeper
intro.text: The echo only borrows your last move for a moment. Use that borrowed beat to cross before the bell fades.

hintTiers: The echo holds the door while you push the parcel onto the teleporter to activate the far switch.
Time the echo to stay on the near switch while you push the parcel through the teleporter to land on the far switch.

Move right to queue echo, wait for it to reach the switch, push parcel right onto teleporter which sends it to back layer switch. Go through both opened doors to the stitch, switch layers, navigate to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine echo timing with dual parcel management and cross-layer teleportation.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players switch too early and forget the echo.

rooms.title: Stamped Exit
rooms.objective: Chain teleporters across three layers to reach the mailbox at the bottom.
rooms.blurb: The clocktower's tube system spans all three sheets of the bell mechanism.

intro.speaker: Bell Keeper
intro.text: The bell tubes connect all three sheets. Each teleporter drops you one layer deeper. Read the chain before you step in.

hintTiers: The teleporters form a chain: layer 0 to layer 1, then layer 1 to layer 2. But walls block direct paths.
Use the first teleporter to reach layer 1, navigate the maze there, use the second teleporter to reach layer 2, then find the mailbox.
Navigate to teleporter at (7,2) on layer 0, warp to layer 1 at (2,5), navigate the middle maze to teleporter at (6,6), warp to layer 2 at (3,2), navigate down and right to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Multi-layer teleporter chains with conveyor belts.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players get disoriented across layers.

rooms.title: Pendulum Route
rooms.objective: Combine echo timing, teleporters, and one-way gates across three layers.
rooms.blurb: A side route that turns one rerouted stitch into a full three-sheet descent.

intro.speaker: Bell Keeper
intro.text: The stamp drops you onto a second stitch if you line the sheets up first. Think of it like a pendulum swing, not a ladder.

hintTiers: The echo must reach the switch via the teleporter while you navigate one-way gates across three layers.
Time the echo to teleport onto the switch, then navigate through one-way gates, use the stitch to layer 2, use a second teleporter to reach the final area.

Move right to queue echo, navigate up through one-way gates while echo teleports to switch. Go through opened door, use stitch to middle layer, navigate to teleporter, warp to layer 2, navigate maze to mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine echo timing with teleporter chains and one-way gates across three layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players forget the final climb.

rooms.title: Understudy
rooms.objective: Guide your shadow to the switch while navigating walls and corridors.
rooms.blurb: The stage mirrors movement even when the audience cannot see it.

intro.speaker: Stagehand
intro.text: Your shadow moves in the opposite direction across its own sheet. Think about where it lands, not where you do.

hintTiers: The shadow mirrors your movement. Every step right sends it left. Plan a path that places it on the switch.
You need to move so the shadow hits the switch while you can still reach the door. The maze layout means not every move is mirrored cleanly.
Move right twice, down once (shadow goes left twice, up once onto the switch). Walk through the opened door and navigate the corridors to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Teach mirrored shadow movement with larger maze and ice wings layer.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players track their own movement but not the shadow.

rooms.title: Latch Cue
rooms.objective: Navigate ice corridors while guiding your shadow to latch the switch across three layers.
rooms.blurb: The stage route stays open once the understudy hits the mark, but ice changes everything.

intro.speaker: Stagehand
intro.text: A latched cue only needs one clean mark. After that, the scene stays set for you.

hintTiers: The shadow must latch the switch while you slide on ice. Ice affects you but not the shadow.
Plan your ice slides so the mirrored shadow movement lands on the latch. Then descend through layers.
Slide right on ice (shadow goes left to switch). Navigate down to stitch, switch to middle layer, descend to lower stitch, switch to layer 2, push parcel to open final path, reach mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine shadow latching with ice physics and three-layer navigation.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players assume the shadow must keep standing on the switch.

rooms.title: Marked Landing
rooms.objective: Guide two shadows through one-way gates to latch two switches simultaneously.
rooms.blurb: The spotlight stamp only helps if both shadows have already unlocked their respective doors.

intro.speaker: Stagehand
intro.text: Two shadows, two marks. Both must hit their cues before the scene opens.

hintTiers: Two shadows mirror you on two different layers. Each must reach its own switch.
Plan a movement sequence that places both shadows on their respective switches while navigating one-way gates.

Move right twice (both shadows go left). Move down once (both go up). Shadow A reaches switch on layer 1, shadow B reaches switch on layer 2. Navigate through both opened doors via one-way gate circuit to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Dual shadow coordination with one-way gates across four layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players plan for one shadow and forget the other.

rooms.title: Backstage Fold
rooms.objective: Combine shadow, echo, and teleporters across three layers for the ultimate stage puzzle.
rooms.blurb: A secret side route that turns one marked landing into a full backstage fold.

intro.speaker: Stagehand
intro.text: The cleanest backstage routes never look like straight lines from the audience. Trust the drop and keep climbing.

hintTiers: The shadow latches one door, the echo holds another, and teleporters connect all three layers.
Move to latch the shadow switch first. Then time the echo to hold the second door while you teleport between layers.

Move right to latch shadow switch. Navigate to echo timing position. Move right to queue echo onto switch via teleporter. Pass through both opened doors. Use teleporter to layer 2. Navigate the final maze to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: The ultimate theater challenge combining shadow, echo, and teleporters.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players keep searching the middle sheet for the goal.

rooms.title: Festival Line
rooms.objective: Use two parcels, a projector, ice, one-way gates, and switches across three layers.
rooms.blurb: This is the first true mixed-mechanic route in the campaign.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: By now the town expects more than one insight at a time. Hold the line open, then build the bridge.

outro.speaker: Mina
outro.text: The higher lanes are back, but three odd little side routes are still missing from the margins.

hintTiers: One parcel for each switch. The projector bridges the gap. One-way gates force a specific circuit.
Push parcel A across ice to the visible switch. Transfer parcel B to the hidden switch. Push the projector into position. Navigate the one-way circuit.
Slide parcel A right on ice to switch at (9,5). Transfer parcel B to back layer switch. Push projector up to bridge the gap on layer 2. Navigate one-way gates through all three layers to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine all previous mechanics.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players solve the bridge first and discover they need the door open.

rooms.title: Forwarded Lantern
rooms.objective: Combine projection, shadow movement, teleporters, and ice across three layers.
rooms.blurb: The rooftop route demands mastery of projection and shadow coordination.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: Projection stamps forward the bridge itself. Line the lantern up with the stamp, not the gap.

hintTiers: The shadow latches a switch while the projector bridges the gap. Teleporters connect the layers.
Move to latch the shadow switch, then push the projector onto ice to slide into position. Use the teleporter to descend.

Move right to latch shadow. Push projector left onto ice, it slides to bridge position. Navigate to teleporter at layer 0, warp to layer 1, descend to stitch, switch to layer 2, cross bridge through opened door to mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine shadow latching, ice-based projector placement, and teleporter chains.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players push the lantern directly under the gap.

rooms.title: Stamped Parcel
rooms.objective: Use two parcels, two switches, and teleporters across three layers to open the final corridor.
rooms.blurb: A transfer stamp can park a parcel exactly where a distant lane needs weight.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: The parcel does not stay where you send it. The rooftop stamp forwards the delivery to the pressure plate.

hintTiers: Each parcel activates a different switch on a different layer. Teleporters help you reach the distant areas.
Transfer one parcel to the back layer switch, push the other across the maze to the visible switch. Use teleporters to navigate between layers.

Transfer parcel A to back layer where it lands on hidden switch. Push parcel B through the maze to visible switch. Use teleporter chain to descend through three layers. Navigate through both opened doors to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Triple parcel management across three layers with teleporter-assisted navigation.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players try to walk the parcel manually.

rooms.title: Sky Postscript
rooms.objective: Combine projector, echo, one-way gates, and ice across three layers for the hidden rooftop note.
rooms.blurb: The skyline keeps one extra route for players who read the stamps and the folds together.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: There is one more note tucked into the skyline if you can read the bridge, the stitch, and the drop as one route.

hintTiers: The projector bridges the gap, the echo holds a door, one-way gates force your circuit. Ice adds momentum.
Push the projector onto ice to slide it into bridge position. Time the echo to hold the door. Navigate the one-way gate circuit through all three layers.

Push projector right onto ice where it slides to bridge position. Navigate one-way loop to echo timing area. Queue echo, wait for it to reach switch. Pass through door, descend via stitches, cross bridge to mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Combine projector, echo timing, ice, and one-way gates.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players forget the bridge was forwarded.

rooms.title: Festival Line Restored
rooms.objective: Master all mechanics across four layers to reconnect the full rooftop delivery line.
rooms.blurb: The final rooftop route ties every mechanic into one grand puzzle across four sheets.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: This is the full line: park the parcel, trust the forwarded bridge, then follow the fold all the way down to the festival roof.

outro.speaker: Mina
outro.text: The festival line is back. If you also found the three hidden margins, there is still one attic route left above us.

hintTiers: Four layers, multiple entities, all mechanics. Solve the setup on layer 0 before descending.
Push parcel onto switch, align projector, latch the shadow switch, then descend through all four layers using stitches and teleporters.

Push parcel to switch at (1,10). Push projector to bridge position. Move to latch shadow. Use top stitch to layer 1, navigate to teleporter, warp to layer 2, use stitch to layer 3, cross bridge through opened doors to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: The ultimate mixed-mechanic challenge across four layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players start climbing before the parcel is parked.

rooms.title: Dustline
rooms.objective: Use shadow, teleporters, ice, and one-way gates across three layers to reach the hidden mailbox.
rooms.blurb: A secret bonus room built around shadow coordination with teleporter shortcuts.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: You found the attic route. The old latch still works, if your shadow can reach it first.

outro.speaker: Mina
outro.text: That was only the first hidden fold. The deeper attic line still waits above the rafters.

hintTiers: The shadow must latch the switch via one-way gates while you navigate ice corridors and teleporters.
Move to place the shadow on the latch via one-way gate routing. Then use the teleporter to descend through layers.

Move right to send shadow left through one-way gate onto latch. Navigate the ice corridor to teleporter. Warp to layer 1, navigate maze to stitch, switch to layer 2, cross through opened door to mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Shadow latching with ice, one-way gates, teleporters, and key/lock across four layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players assume the shadow must keep standing on the switch.

rooms.title: Folded Ledger
rooms.objective: Combine shadow, echo, two parcels, and all mechanics across three layers.
rooms.blurb: One hidden route folds through complex machinery requiring every skill learned.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: The attic routes are never straight. Open the top door with your shadow first, then trust the drop into the ledger fold.

hintTiers: Shadow latches one door, echo holds another, both parcels must reach their switches. Everything happens across three layers.
Latch the shadow switch first. Time the echo for the second door. Transfer one parcel, push the other. Descend via stitches and teleporters.

Move right to latch shadow. Navigate to echo timing area, queue it toward switch via teleporter. Transfer parcel A to back layer switch. Push parcel B to visible switch. Descend through all three layers to the mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: Full-mechanic challenge with gravity, conveyors, and key/lock across four layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players set the shadow correctly but keep searching the wrong sheet.

rooms.title: Mina's Postscript
rooms.objective: Solve the ultimate puzzle using every mechanic across four layers.
rooms.blurb: The hidden route ends by combining every mechanic the game has taught.

intro.speaker: Mina
intro.text: This is the one route I never wrote down cleanly. Set the shadow cue, trust the drop, and let the lantern finish the sentence.

hintTiers: Four layers, shadow, projector, teleporters, ice, one-way gates. Everything converges here.
Shadow latches door on layer 1. Projector bridges gap on layer 3. Ice and one-way gates control your path. Teleporters connect the layers.

Move right to latch shadow. Push projector onto ice to bridge position on layer 3. Navigate one-way circuit to top stitch. Descend: layer 1 stitch to layer 2, teleporter to layer 3, cross bridge through opened door to mailbox.

balance.intendedLesson: The ultimate finale combining every mechanic across four layers.
balance.commonMisunderstanding: Players forget the lantern bridge is being rerouted.

demo.title: Festival Route Demo

ending.title: Demo Route Complete
ending.subtitle: The greenhouse line is lit and the festival preview route is back in circulation.
ending.body: The full campaign pushes the same paper-layer rules into delayed echoes, mirrored shadows, and a final rooftop delivery lane.

beat.speaker: Mina
beat.text: That is the last lantern route for the demo. Next come bell echoes, stage shadows, and the rooftop line itself.

teaserLines: Clocktower: Echo couriers repeat your previous move one beat later.
Theater: Shadow couriers mirror you across a second sheet.
Rooftops: Doors, bridges, and transfers braid into one final lane.

journalEntries.title: Bell Margin
journalEntries.body: The bell routes were stamped to drop tired couriers onto lower ledges. Mina says good routing saves effort you never see.

journalEntries.title: Backstage Margin
journalEntries.body: The theater keeps one folded route behind the scenery so stagehands can move props without crossing the audience's eye line.

journalEntries.title: Sky Margin
journalEntries.body: The skyline note was never meant for deliveries. Mina used it to leave messages where only someone climbing the roofs would read them.

journalEntries.title: Attic Margin
journalEntries.body: The first attic page lists route pieces Mina hid on purpose, just to see who still noticed the folds after the credits rolled.

journalEntries.title: Mina's Postscript
journalEntries.body: The town was never broken into separate routes. It was one folded letter the whole time, waiting for someone patient enough to read every crease.

ending.title: Festival Line Restored
ending.subtitle: The rooftop delivery line is live again and the town reads like one folded letter.
ending.body: Credits are safe without the secret route. The attic still waits for anyone who found every hidden margin note on the way up.

beat.speaker: Mina
beat.text: That is the line the town needed. If you also found the three margin routes, meet me in the attic.

ending.title: Secret Line Complete
ending.subtitle: The attic postscript is open and Mina's hidden route finally has a reader.
ending.body: Every late-game side route now folds back into one final attic line, turning the optional mastery path into the game's quietest ending.

beat.speaker: Mina
beat.text: Most postkeepers stop at the official route. You kept reading until the margins answered back.
